commits.message:
Fix range-check code.

Trivial typo caused compiler to assert when pointer was valid, rather than
on the NULL value.

Fix type compatibility for array types.

The type compatibility would accept any non-array type as compatible with
an array. This was due to a logic error in the CompatibleType function
where it would return the array type if the type wasn't an array.

This patch rearranges the return values in the CompatibleType function.

No change intended for valid Pascal programs, but some class of errors
are now caught that would previously not be detected.

A test case added to check that this is caught.

Error on assignment of the result of divide and power to integer

The compiler would allow and compile something like

var a: integer;
...
  a := 2 / 5;
...

It would then store a double value into the integer variable, potentially
overwriting the next variable after. This is not allowed in Pascal, should
either use the div or some variant of conversion to integer.

Basic test cases added.

No change to valid Pascal code, this only affects code that was not
going to work correctly anyway.

Add back llvmversion file

This allows building the LLVM that is required for the compiler.

Fix makefile to rebuild the llvmversion file every time.
Use C++ header instead of C header

[NFC] Dump the built-in function name and arguments

Debug dumps of builtin functions were not showing what builtin functionality
was being used, or what the arguments were to the function. This adds a dump
function for the builtin function base class, that shows the name and the
arguments of the function.

This is only really useful for debugging, so no functional change.

Update LLVM to more recent LLVM version.

Mainly removing type information from calls to llvm::PointerType::getUnqual
and passing theContext instead. A small change to make sure the llvm type
information is generated when using forward-declared (opaque) types, as
that happened as a side-effect of generating pointer type info before.

Some APIs changed to do with targetmachine has changed, and thus been
updated.

Add further checks in CheckProtoMatch to check VAR parameter

Make sure the repeated definition of a function matches the original
declaration with respect to the VAR.

Also mark this as "done" in the objects.txt todo-list.

Check function definition matches declaration.

Forward declared functions could be defined with different
argument types than the orirignal declaration. It would
still use the original declartion, but with some weird effects
for certain situation.

Also, semantics would accept real value for integer parameters,
leading to an assert for mismatched arguments in LLVM.

[NFC] Remove more useless includes

Multiple places include more than they actually need. Some
completely without use, others just need a forward declaration of some
type(s).
Update improvement todo list

Pass a result string into the runtime trim function.

This should reduce the amount of string copying required to return
the string.

[NFC] Remove uses of true/false as arguments.

Use enums instead of booleans. In one case, pass in a type declaration
instead of boolean.

This is just to avoid having smatterings of true/false that determine
the path through a function, and make it a bit clearer what that extra
argument does.

This is not changing any functionality in the compiler, just tidying
things up.

Add support of for in array

The compiler now supports a similar concept to the C++ container
iterators, using the same style as for in set.
Add missed test
Remove useless if/else, just call MakeAddresable
Remove useless checks for alloca failing

Add check for integer on width and precision of writes.

This used to be checked in the expr.cpp with code-gen. Bring it up to
semantics.
Add a bit more testing for write enums

Allow writing enums as string values.

Implement a new runtime function that finds the name of an enum in a table
and writes the string.

Simple test added.

[NFC] Remove some unnecessary includes.

Don't include constants and types into lexer.h and lexer.cpp - they
aren't used in either place.

Fix initializing character arrays with single character

One of the tests in the iso10206-tests suite hit an assert. Fix it by
special-casing single character initialisation of arrays.

This bug was introduced in commit 0fc91a5f, Jul 6th 2024.

Adding a new test to avoid regressing this again.

Remove unnecessary variable declarations.

Simplify some arguments being passed in various places.

Also add const to a place or two.

No functional change.

Update to LLVM 20

No functional change, just some minor updates to make the code compile
again.
Add minimal support for module

Add support for setting the random seed witn randomize

Randomize now either sets the seed to the current time in seconds
or the integer argument given.

Add tests to check that random numbers are different for different seed.

Add randomize builtin function.

This sets the seed for the random generator based on the current time in
seconds.

Some support for handling pointer address compares.

This is not finished, just committing some work to improve things towards
that functionality.

Support different size index values in different parts of an array

Multidimensional arrays need to use the same index type in the flattened
1D array is ultimately generated.

This finds the largest type and uses that for the index type, rather than
the type of the type of the individual ranges describing the index. This
means LLVM won't assert when trying to multiply a constant of type i8 by a
constant of type i32.

No real functional change, just unifying types.

Update some AST definitions.

Preparing for proper function pointer usage by tidying up a few things
and making CallExprAST derive from AddressableAST.

[NFC] Add support to dump AST during compilation.

This option allows debugging of the compilation process by printing the
AST to stderr.

Use -emit=ast to request AST dumping. The compiler will quit at the end
of dumping the AST.
[NFC] Reduce scope of variable

[NFC] Remove constant type argument on CharExprAST constructor.

No functional change, just don't pass type for character expressions
to the constructor.

[NFC] Remove always same parameter to RealExprAST constructor.

Simplifies the calling code, no functional change.

Add support to read bool as text

When using the read (or readln) function, a bool can be read.

Support more conversions to complex

Also seapate the handling of divide and power operations. They are almost
the same, but not quite, so make it two separate cases.

[NFC] Use switch/case instead of sequence of if-statements in semantics

The semantics ccheck for BinaryExpr was using a long set of if statements
to determine what was going on. This changes some of those if-statements
to switch/case.

No functional change.

Support array of char as initializers for arrays.

This is an ISO10206 feature missed when implementing array initializers,
which supported strings, but not char arrays.
Improve dumping of InitArrayAST

Allow initializer values for variant types.

This is not complete, but it prevents the compiler from erroring out during
parsing on such constructs. The initializer code-gen still needs to be
updated.

Add support for ** (power operator) in constant expressions.

The ISO10206 standard allows constant expressions that contain ** as
an operator. This patch adds support for this.
Remove redundant Constants:: in constants.cpp

Add support for constant pow calculations.

The ISO10206 standard allows pow to be used in constant expressions,
e.g. const eight = 2 pow 3;
This adds support for that functionality.

Honour "protected" attribute on variable arguments

ISO10206 says we shouldn't be able to assign to protected function
arguments. So check that, and report an error when that happens.

Support complex and real types, as per specification for POW operator

The ISO10206 specification states that POW can be used for REAL and
COMPLEX types, as well as integer types.

This implementation simply calls the same REAL or COMPLEX solution as
the ** operator for these cases.

Add a couple of tests to check that it works.
Add static to ComplexBinExpr function

Improve error checking for binary expressions

Only accept numericy types for the four standard operators.

Only integer and boolen for AND, OR and XOR.

This prevents hitting an ICE when trying to generate the code.

Add more ICE_IF instead of asserts.

This ensures the compiler exits with a message rather than crashing
if something goes wrong.

Some other minor changes, no functional change besides release build
not crashing badly on failures [at least in theory].

Add ICE_IF that checks a condition and calls ICE if the condition is true

This reduces the amount of code like if (something) ICE(...).

No functional change.

Fix trim runtime function and widen support for string concatenation

The trim function wasn't correctly removing spaces at end of strings,
and didn't correctly calculate the new length correctly. These issues
are now fixed.

Having a character array and concatenating it to a string wasn't
working. Add code to support that.

Add proper internal compiler error mechanism.

Code was previously relying on asserts to avoid crashing when something
has gone wrong internally (e.g. unimplemneted features).

Remove several return 0 statemnets, and replace with ICE.

No functional change intended.
Fix broken test

Support character array for trim operations.

This is of course what it was originally designed to be used for, but the
previous implementation was a bit broken.

New test added in the newstringfunctions test file.

A bug was also found in comparing character arrays. This was fixed
at the same time, and a new regression test added

Support for printing sliced strings per ISO10206.

Passing a section of string as a character array, and correctly
handle the length of the newly created sub-string.

Improve tracing and remove redundant check.

Add TRACE macros to a few more places.

Remove "greter than 2" check for BothStringish function, as it is
entirely redundant.

Improve support for ISO10206 string functionality

Allow range-types and integer types to both be used for indexing
in a "slice".

Allow range-types for substr operands.

Allow dynamic arrays to be identified as  Char Arrays.

No functional change other than accepting a wider range of
source code patterns.

Add support for schemas on sets.

This impklements the schema support for set of ..., including a simple
test for it.

Part of the ISO10206 standard.

Optimise readint64 a little bit

Instead of callling the indirect function twice in places, store
the result of the call in a local variable and reuse.

This saves approximately 25% of the time on reading a large file of
integer values.
Fix type checking for schemas

Add support for basic schema array declarations.

This is part of the ISO10206 standard, and now supports at
least simple array declarations of the type:

   type sa(n:integer) = array [1..n] of integer;
   var  arr: sa(100);  // 100 element array.

Added very basic test.

Change ArrayDecl and ArrayExpr to use RangeBaseDecl instead of RangeDecl

This will allow the SchemaRange to be be used for Arrays.

No functional change intended.

Add file/line info in verbose mode for Error printing in parser

This helps identify (sometimes at least), where in the parser an
error came from.

No functional change intended.

Add more schema support.

Now supporting both one and two values for rangeh declarations.

Adding basic test too.

Add very simple schema parsing.

This supports the "template" system in ISO-10206 Pascal, but only
for the most simple of use-case: range with a constant start and
a variable end value.

This is by no means a functional implementation, but committed
as a basic starting point, to avoid having a very big change
all at once.
Update llvmversion again
Fix up for moving to newer llvm
Update to latest LLVM

Do not cast things to what they already are.

Sometimes when converting real/integer to complex, the compiler
generates two TypeCast operations. The second one will incorrectly
convert the complex number to the real value + 0.0i.

This patch fixes this and corrects the expected result as well.

Refactor semantics for binary expression checking

The code was quite complex, so split it out into a separate function.

It's still quite messy, but adding early returns makes it a little easier
to follow at least.

No functional change intended.

Reduce number of boiler-plate virtual functions on types

Make separate, rather the virtual member functions for some of the
trivial boolean values and such.

Some functions were not really used in a particularly useful way, so
could be completely removed and replaced - Bits for example can be
substituted with a call to Size() * CHAR_BIT.

This reduces the code size by some fair amount, and I think it makes
it easier to follow too.

No functional change intended.

[NFC] Refactor CodeGen for VarDeclAST into two functions

One for Global Variables, one for Local variables in functions
and procedures.

Some other minor changes, like passing args as const reference
rather than by value in some constructors.

No functional change.

Fix up GetOutput/GetInput

Unify into one function, rather than having two almost identical
functions.

[NFC] Simplify code by returning early in ParseVariableExpr

Instead of repeatedly check if expr has been set, return whenever
the result is determined.

Also small simplificatiion in ParseCallOrVariableExpr.

No functioncal change.

[NFCI] Tidy up some bits of VariableExprAST handling

Remove unused constructor. Add a new constructor for NamedObject.
Do not base FunctionExprAST on VariableExprAST, as it uses none
of its content or functionality.

Clean up some unused variables in the parser, remove nunnecessary
function argument.

No functional change intended.

Introduce functions to make VariableExprAST for Input and Output

This is used for I/O functions. This is a first part of changing
this so that the input and output variables can be "hidde" by
local variables.
Do not call visit twice in FunctionAST

Change index for ArrayInit to be int64_t just in case.

Unlikely that anyone sensibly will use more than 2G in an index,
but let's at least not do weird things IF someone tries.

Use multi-argument llvm::isa<...> instead of oring several isa

Instead of if (llvm::isa<A>(x) || llvm::isa<B>(x)) use
if (llvm::isa<A, B>(x)).

No Funcntional Change Intended.

Add check for non-integer initializer index.

Instead of hitting an assert inside Constants::ToInt, check the
type, and report an error when an index is not integral type.

Add support for constant arrays as initializers.

Another ISO10206 concept.

Add support for otherwise in array initialization

This allows "all other elements" to be initialized in an array
with a single value.

An ISO10206 feature.

Support for alternative type initializer

Named types can be initialized with t=name[values] rather than
t=name value [values]. This adds support for parsing that format.

An ISO10206 feature.

Add support for sizeof constants.

Another improvement to constant values, allow sizeof to be used
as a constant expression.

Error when precision is provided on non-real arguments

The second colon and number in write is only allowed on real type
values. This checks for the value type and reports an error if
there's a precision argument for a non-real type.

New test added for this case too.

Add int function to truncate real value into its integer value

This works the same way as trunc, except the result is a REAL
value, where trunk makes an integer.

Add constant functions for frac, int, trunc, rouna and odd

These allow some more constant declarations to be made - all
functions behave the same as their runtime variants.

Add frac built-in function

The frac function returns the fraction part of a floating point value.

Also removed a couple of unused functions - the builtin function
calls directly to the C runtim library, so removed the wrapper
functions.

Add more constant operators: and, or, xor, shr and shl

Also update the modulo operator to simplify things.

Reject types and other none-variable names when for variable expressions

This avoids a later error where the variable isn't found (because
there is no such variable).

Add initializer for pointer types.

This change allows a pointer to be initialized with a value of NIL. No
other value is valid.

Change behaviour of constant divide.

In constant expressions, the result of the '/' operator was keeping
the type, so 12/7 would result in a value of 1, rather than 1.714-something.

This introduces the DIV and MOD operators for constant values.

Update tests to reflect this change in behaviour, including an additonal
test for the MOD operation.

Move constant function evaluation to constants.cpp

The evaluation and creation of new constants from constant functions
is more to do with constant handling than parsing, so move it into
the source file that deals with constants.

This also moves a couple of other functions, and making a helper function
that identifies constant functions, and moving the ConstDeclToInt function
into the same file.

No functional change intended.

[NFC] Format several files.

Quite a number of  formatting errors had crept in, so fixing those as a
separate commit here.

Add support for some constant functions

This adds support for succ, pred, ord, length, sin, cos, ln and exp as
functions for generating constants.

Simplify some token handling and fix location stupidity.

We only ever use PeekToken().GetToken(), so include the GetToken()
in the function. NextToken() was only using the resturned value in
two places. So make it a void function and use CurrentToken() for
the other uses.

Semantics: Check that condition on while, if and repeat is boolean

It is an error to use a non-boolean expression as the condition
in while, repeat .. until and if. Previously this would lead
to a crash in LLVM. Now we show a diagnostic message, which
makes it easier to understand what is wrong.

Also fixed a few missing "visit" calls for the visitor pattern,
including the ones for repeat and while.

Generated code for valid input source code is unchanged.

Add tests for invalid arguments to some functions

The chr and odd functions should not accept character types
for input. The code already checks that, but no testing was
done to ensure it doesn't break.

[NFC] Use auto for result of dyn_cast.

No point in doing T* name = llvm::dyn_cast<T>(x), when we can
use auto and avoid repeating those types.

No functional change.

Add support for some more types of ISO10206 constant declarations.

Allow constant sets and constant functions - currently only supporting
`chr(constant)`.

Fix broken code

Running ISO10206 tests showed a couple of bugs had crept in with the past
few changes.

This fixes those and adds tests to avoid those things being broken again.
Note that the bind test currently doesn't actually work. It is still
not clear to me exactly how bind is meant to work.

Also added a line to the improvement-todo.txt to remind myself that the
error recovery definitely should be improved, so there isn't a lot of error
messages from one small mistake.
